run_findings.mcp_2026_list_semantics: MCP 2026-07-28 declares tools.listChanged and tools/list as current client-specific enumeration; modern list-change delivery uses subscriptions/listen. No list generation token binds a later tools/call, so notifications are invalidation/freshness signals rather than exclusive-action preconditions.
run_findings.inspector_counterexample_scope: Official Inspector issue #1920 documented a tools-only modern-era client that failed to open subscriptions/listen despite tools.listChanged=true. It was opened 2026-08-05 and closed completed 2026-08-11; retained only as exact historical evidence that server advertisement alone did not prove client notification handling in affected builds.
run_findings.github_mcp_effective_capability: GitHub MCP Server read-only/exclude precedence changes effective tools; lockdown is not authorization. Classic PAT scope filtering can hide tools, while fine-grained PAT/GitHub App/server tokens show tools and rely on API enforcement; scope-fetch failure degrades to no filtering. Tool visibility does not prove authorization across auth modes.
run_findings.kubernetes_mcp_stale_capability: Kubernetes MCP Server supports read_only/destructive/tool/target filters and SIGHUP registry rebuild; stateless=true disables tool/prompt change notifications, creating a documented stale-enumeration hazard.
